subject.title: Gateway WebSocket connections leak - CLOSE_WAIT/FIN_WAIT_2 zombie connections cause crashes

question: Should maintainers queue a narrow Gateway missed-pong cleanup from the source gap now, or require live Windows socket-state/crash proof before implementation work proceeds?
rationale: Source inspection confirms a stale-peer cleanup gap, but the reported crash impact is Windows-specific and overlaps adjacent Gateway crash reports, so automation should not choose the root-cause boundary or proof bar.

options.title: Keep live-repro triage
options.body: Retain this as the canonical issue while waiting for Windows netstat/fatal-report proof before queueing a fix PR.

options.title: Queue narrow stale-peer cleanup
options.body: Treat missed-pong termination as independently valuable and ask for a focused Gateway handler/test fix while leaving crash causality unresolved.

options.title: Fold into Windows crash triage
options.body: Move the crash discussion to the broader Windows Gateway crash family only if maintainers decide the socket states are a symptom rather than a separate lifecycle bug.

recommendation.title: Keep live-repro triage
recommendation.body: Retain this as the canonical issue while waiting for Windows netstat/fatal-report proof before queueing a fix PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway lifecycle work in the same handler makes steipete the best available owner for deciding the proof bar and fix boundary.
